submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole is the saturated-inhibition readout (GeLU floor ~0.17) of an L1 neuron: it peaks on non-sequence-initial, word-initial tokens whose embedding plus local bigram context do not match the neuron's positive key (e.g. senator, pleaded, boils, at, summit, the cat/dog). It is silent on the sequence-initial token (which drives the positive pole instead), on continuation pieces and veto words with opposing unigram keys (iked, announced, degrees, rose, world, me, defendant), with the same token's strength varying strongly by predecessor (to: 0.17 after According vs 0.03 after hiked).

adversarial_test_results.detail: Position control: claimed trigger 'senator' as the sequence-initial token must be silent per the hypothesis.
Position control: claimed trigger 'guilty' as the sequence-initial token must be silent despite being an activating token elsewhere.
Token-type control: a single long word is only a sequence-initial piece plus continuation pieces, both silent classes, so nothing should fire.
Bigram suppression: 'to' after 'hiked' is the hypothesis's own weak case (0.03 vs 0.17 after According), so with 'hiked' initial the whole probe should stay silent.
Veto-word control: sequence-initial 'defendant' is silent by position and 'announced' is a claimed veto word, so no token should fire.
Veto-word control with a novel carrier: initial 'she' is silent by position and 'announced' is a veto unigram key.
Veto-word control: initial 'world' is silent by position and 'rose' carries an opposing unigram key.
Veto-word control: initial 'rose' is silent by position and 'degrees' is a claimed veto word.
Veto-word control: initial 'degrees' is silent by position and 'me' is a claimed veto word.
Veto-word control in example-like context: initial 'The' is silent by position and 'defendant' is a veto word.
Continuation-piece control: 'unhappiness' tokenizes into an initial piece plus continuation pieces, all silent classes under the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Minutes of the quarterly water board session, convened Tuesday morning in the civic annex north wing with all five commissioners present plus staff counsel and the clerk. The chair called the meeting to order at nine sharp and asked for approval of the agenda, which passed without objection after a brief correction to item four regarding pipe inspections along Cedar Avenue. The operations manager then presented the monthly flow report, noting steady reservoir levels, normal pump station output, and two minor valve repairs completed ahead of schedule near the Elm Street junction. Questions from commissioners focused on overtime hours logged during the overnight main break, and staff promised a detailed breakdown before the next workshop. The finance officer summarized quarterly expenditures, highlighting savings from the joint purchasing agreement for meters, chemicals, and fleet maintenance, and flagged one overage tied to emergency contractor fees that will be offset next quarter. Public comment followed, with three residents speaking in favor of extended splash pad hours, one landlord asking about backflow testing deadlines, and a student group presenting a poster on storm drain stenciling. The board thanked each speaker and directed staff to post testing reminders online and at the library. Under old business, members reviewed the hydrant flushing calendar, confirmed dates for the fall open house, and accepted the audit committee recommendation to rotate inspection zones starting in January. New business opened with a proposal to replace aging telemetry units at four wells, and after discussion of vendor quotes, warranty terms, and installation windows, the board authorized staff to negotiate a final purchase order. A second item covered the shared internship program with the technical college, which drew praise for pipeline training and weekend coverage, and the board voted to renew it for another year. The communications lead outlined plans for a newsletter insert explaining winter shutoff protections, billing options, and conservation rebates, with drafts due for review at the October workshop. Commissioners then discussed travel approvals for the spring utility conference, the regional planning forum in November, and a peer exchange visit hosted by the neighboring district, agreeing to send two delegates to each gathering and to circulate notes afterward. The clerk read upcoming filing deadlines into the record, staff confirmed calendar invitations for committee check-ins, and the chair reminded everyone that budget worksheets are due before the retreat. With no further items, members set the next regular meeting date, confirmed the venue, and adjourned after directing staff to circulate the final summit agenda.
